ident.purpose: The CLIP2POD station mark in the header. Largest, most-tracked element; appears once.

control.purpose: Button faces. Mono 11px uppercase, 0.1em tracking; the kbd shortcut floats right at 9px.

label.purpose: Band and sidebar headers, field captions, table headers, dialog titles, settings subsections, the lamp word, segmented-cell faces. Mono 10px uppercase, 0.14em, muted.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy inside dialogs. System sans 14px / 1.5.

prose.purpose: The article in the CodeMirror editor. System sans 13.5px / 1.5 — the only place the user's own words live.

field.purpose: Input text, dialog code blocks, the RIP queue job title. Mono 13px.

data.purpose: Table cell text, toast body, coach-bar text, the junk textarea. Mono 12.5px.

note.purpose: Dialog hint/check rows, the RIP doctor strip, the settings detected-version line. Sans 12px.

kbd.purpose: The kbd chip on a button face. Mono 9px, 0.72 opacity.

shadows.name: floating-panel
shadows.purpose: The coach bar and toasts — a small element lifted just off the desk.

shadows.name: modal-lift
shadows.purpose: The dialog panel — a larger throw for a larger overlay, over a shadow-filled backdrop.

motion.name: overlay-entrance
motion.purpose: Coach bar, modal, and toast entrances (160-180ms) and the render rail's ease toward each chunk mark (400ms).

motion.name: control-transition
motion.purpose: Button border-color and background on hover; segmented-cell text colour.

motion.name: lamp-state
motion.purpose: Status-lamp bulb background and halo when the desk changes state.

motion.name: onair-pulse
motion.purpose: The ON AIR / RENDERING / RIPPING lamp bulb halo, echoed by the NARRATE queue bar's rendering-item disc. Dropped under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: progress-fill
motion.purpose: The determinate RIP progress bar's scaleX toward the reported percent.

motion.name: indeterminate-stripes
motion.purpose: The RIP progress bar's barber-pole background-position slide before a percent is known. Reduced-motion freezes the slide but keeps the stripes.

components.name: Default Button
components.description: Every secondary control on the desk - transport, tools, dialog actions, and now the header FEED/LOG/SETTINGS. Left-aligned mono face with an optional shortcut floated right.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: block; width: 100%; text-align: left; font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; background: #262a60; color: #e9e9ed; border: 1px solid rgba(233,233,237,0.16); border-radius: 4px; padding: 7px 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 120ms, background 120ms; } .ds-btn kbd { float: right; font-family: inherit; font-size: 9px; opacity: 0.72; margin-left: 10px; } .ds-btn:hover { border-color: #6f63b0; } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b5abfc; outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Exactly one per view - Generate MP3 on NARRATE, Download on RIP, the confirming action in a dialog footer.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: block; width: 100%; text-align: left; font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; background: #b5abfc; color: #161826; border: 1px solid #b5abfc; border-radius: 4px; padding: 7px 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 120ms; } .ds-btn-primary kbd { float: right; font-family: inherit; font-size: 9px; opacity: 0.72; margin-left: 10px; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b5abfc; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Field
components.description: URL intakes, meta-bar fields, dialog search boxes, the yt-dlp args textarea. Recessed on the deepest tonal layer.
components.css: .ds-field { width: 100%; background: #161826; color: #e9e9ed; border: 1px solid rgba(233,233,237,0.16); border-radius: 4px; padding: 6px 8px; font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 13px; } .ds-field::placeholder { color: #9b9bb8; opacity: 1; } .ds-field:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b5abfc; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: The header mode toggle (NARRATE / RIP) and the author-gender control (UNK / M / F). One bordered box, borderless cells, active cell carries aria-pressed and flips to the accent. On the author-gender control, the active cell also gets a 2px currentColor inset ring when its value came from the recognized-authors table rather than a leftover sticky default. Not an ARIA tablist - a group of toggle buttons.
components.css: .ds-seg { display: inline-flex; border: 1px solid rgba(233,233,237,0.16); border-radius: 4px; overflow: hidden; height: 31px; } .ds-seg-cell { font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 0 14px; background: #262a60; color: #9b9bb8; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: color 120ms; } .ds-seg-cell:hover { color: #e9e9ed; } .ds-seg-cell[aria-pressed="true"] { background: #b5abfc; color: #161826; } .ds-seg-cell:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b5abfc; outline-offset: -2px; }

components.name: Status Lamp
components.description: One lamp reads BOTH workers. Bulb: idle grey / signal lavender when queued / danger red with a 1.4s pulse when rendering. The word names the live worker: RENDERING, RIPPING, or ON AIR (both), else QUEUED n or IDLE.
components.css: .ds-lamp { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; min-width: 108px; padding: 6px 12px; background: #262a60; border: 1px solid rgba(233,233,237,0.16); border-radius: 4px; font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #9b9bb8; } .ds-lamp-bulb { width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 50%; background: #3a3d5c; transition: background 200ms, box-shadow 200ms; } .ds-lamp[data-state="queued"] .ds-lamp-bulb { background: #b5abfc; box-shadow: 0 0 8px #b5abfc; } .ds-lamp[data-state="queued"] .ds-lamp-word { color: #b5abfc; } .ds-lamp[data-state="onair"] .ds-lamp-bulb { background: #ef5b6a; box-shadow: 0 0 10px #ef5b6a; animation: ds-onair 1.4s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-lamp[data-state="onair"] .ds-lamp-word { color: #ef5b6a; } @keyframes ds-onair { 50% { box-shadow: 0 0 3px #ef5b6a; opacity: 0.75; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-lamp[data-state="onair"] .ds-lamp-bulb { animation: none; box-shadow: 0 0 12px #ef5b6a; } }

components.name: Desk Band
components.description: The shared layout primitive on both desks. A full-width panel region, band padding, a 1px line bottom border, NO radius. Bands butt together with no gutter; the last band takes flex:1 and its inner list/table owns the scroll.
components.css: .ds-band { display: block; padding: 12px 16px; background: #1d1f3d; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(233,233,237,0.16); } .ds-band-head { margin: 0; font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; color: #9b9bb8; } .ds-band-body { margin-top: 8px; color: #e9e9ed; }

components.name: Doctor Strip
components.description: RIP-only. Shown while yt-dlp / ffmpeg is missing. Neutral panel-raised chrome carrying ONE 6px danger dot - it informs, it does not shout. Commands are user-select:all code; a rip only fails when actually attempted.
components.html: Install yt-dlp to rip audio. Not on your PATH yet - narration still works without it.winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp
components.css: .ds-doctor { display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px 12px; padding: 9px 16px; background: #262a60; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(233,233,237,0.16); font-family: system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #e9e9ed; } .ds-doctor-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: #ef5b6a; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-doctor code { font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 11.5px; background: #1d1f3d; border: 1px solid rgba(233,233,237,0.10); border-radius: 4px; padding: 1px 6px; user-select: all; } .ds-btn-small { font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; background: #262a60; color: #e9e9ed; border: 1px solid rgba(233,233,237,0.16); border-radius: 4px; padding: 3px 8px; cursor: pointer; }

components.name: Coach Bar
components.description: NARRATE only. A floating pill centred 14px above the deck's bottom edge - the junk-review conversation, replacing itself as the review advances, cleared on Escape.
components.html: Junk: “Getty Images”
components.css: .ds-coach { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; background: #262a60; border: 1px solid #6f63b0; border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 14px; font-family: system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 12.5px; color: #e9e9ed; box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(10,10,20,0.55); white-space: nowrap; animation: ds-coach-in 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-coach-btn { font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; background: #262a60; color: #e9e9ed; border: 1px solid rgba(233,233,237,0.16); border-radius: 4px; padding: 5px 10px; cursor: pointer; } @keyframes ds-coach-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(4px); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-coach { animation-name: ds-fade; } } @keyframes ds-fade { from { opacity: 0; } }

components.name: Toast
components.description: Bottom-right stack. ok green marker by default, danger red for errors (which also carry a visually-hidden 'Error:' prefix). Slides in 12px from the right.
components.html: Error: The page produced no readable text
components.css: .ds-toast { position: relative; max-width: 340px; background: #262a60; border: 1px solid rgba(233,233,237,0.16); border-radius: 4px; padding: 9px 14px 9px 28px; font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 12.5px; color: #e9e9ed; box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(10,10,20,0.55); animation: ds-toast-in 180ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-toast-dot { position: absolute; left: 12px; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: #5fd0a0; } .ds-toast[data-kind="error"] .ds-toast-dot { background: #ef5b6a; } .ds-vh { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); } @keyframes ds-toast-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(12px); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-toast { animation-name: ds-fade; } } @keyframes ds-fade { from { opacity: 0; } }

narrative.overview:
The palette is a dark studio by default - deep indigo panels stacked by lightness, one soft lavender that means signal (the lamp when queued, the primary action, the render rail) and one red that means failure (a job that failed, a render in progress, a destructive confirm). Type does the rest of the work: a monospace voice for every control, label, and data readout, uppercased and letter-spaced like console silkscreen, with a plain system sans reserved for the two places real prose lives - the article in the editor and the body copy inside dialogs. The result is dense, calm, and legible at a glance, the way a mixing desk is: you learn the surface once and then operate it without looking.

The desk does two jobs, chosen by a segmented toggle in the header. NARRATE is the script desk: a metadata strip, a large editor with a control column beside it, a queue rail pinned to the bottom. RIP is the same desk configured for pulling a video's audio track: an intake band, a bounded queue, and an episode table that fills the rest of the frame and scrolls inside its own borders. The ident, the lamp, and the FEED / LOG / SETTINGS buttons are shared; only the working surface below them changes. One console, two intake paths.

This is a keyboard-first instrument on the NARRATE side - every primary action shows its shortcut on its own face, and the whole app can be summoned and fed from a global hotkey. Motion is limited to state (a lamp pulse, a rail easing toward the next chunk, a dialog rising 6px) and never to ornament.
keyCharacteristics: Both tabs are the same fixed desk: the window is exactly the viewport, overflow: hidden, and only inner regions (the editor, the sidebar, the queue, the episode table, a dialog body) ever scroll.
One shared header - ident, NARRATE / RIP segmented toggle, one combined status lamp, FEED / LOG / SETTINGS - over a content area that shows one tab's desk at a time.
Monospace, uppercase, letter-spaced type for all chrome; system sans only for authored prose.
One accent (Signal Lavender) for signal, one red for failure, everything else neutral indigo.
Tonal depth: surfaces separate by lightness step, not by shadow. Shadows mark only floating layers.
A single circular-marker vocabulary - the lamp bulb, the toast dot, the queue-item disc, the doctor strip's dot - tinted to state.
Every NARRATE control wears its keyboard shortcut.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Lavender is the only chromatic accent in the chrome. It marks exactly one primary action per view and the live-signal surfaces (lamp, render rail, active segmented cell, focus). If a second passive thing on screen is lavender, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Failure-Is-Red Rule
rules.body: Red is earned by failure: a job that failed, a render in progress (a job that could fail), a destructive confirm. It is never the colour of a warning or an unmet prerequisite. The RIP 'install yt-dlp' strip is neutral panel-raised chrome carrying a single 6px danger dot - the dot signals attention, the card does not shout. Red arrives only when a rip actually fails.

rules.name: The State-Colour Rule
rules.body: Red, green, and the lamp's idle grey are earned by state, never chosen for decoration. Green always means done. A control is never red or green at rest.

rules.name: The Light-Theme Note
rules.body: --muted is the colour of the 10px engraved labels - the smallest text in the app - so it carries the tightest contrast budget. When adjusting a light-theme token, check it against both --bg and white --panel and hold 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Monospace is the chrome; system sans is the content. There is no third face and no in-between use. If new text is a label, a control, a status, or a number, it is mono and uppercase. If it is a sentence the user reads for meaning, it is sans.

rules.name: The Silkscreen Rule
rules.body: All-caps mono chrome always carries tracking - 0.1em on controls, 0.14em on labels, 0.22em on the ident. Uppercased mono without letter-spacing is a bug.

rules.name: The Fixed-Desk Rule
rules.body: The window is always exactly the viewport, overflow: hidden, and this holds for both tabs. New content finds room inside an existing band's own scroll region - the editor, the sidebar, the queue strip, the job list, the episode table, a dialog body. It never makes the window scroll and never adds a fifth band.

rules.name: The Fixed Column Rule
rules.body: The NARRATE control column is exactly 280px (grown from 240px once "Manage Author Genders" needed the room to keep its kbd shortcut on one line; the default window width grew by the same 40px). Full-width buttons stacked in labelled groups; they do not reflow into a grid or change width with the window.

rules.name: The Flat-Desk Rule
rules.body: Anything that is part of the fixed frame - header, desk bands, sidebar, buttons, queue bar, tables, the doctor strip - is flat: tonal fill plus border, zero shadow. Shadow is reserved for the three things that overlay the desk (modals, coach bar, toasts).

rules.name: The Sharp-Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius never exceeds 8px, and only the modal reaches it. Desk bands get no radius at all. If a new surface wants a rounder corner, it is trying to look friendly - and this desk is equipment.

rules.name: The Band-Not-Card Rule
rules.body: Content on either desk lives in full-width bands divided by line, never in inset rounded cards with gaps between them. A card with a shadow or an 8px corner floating in a gutter is a different product.

rules.name: The Circle-Means-Status Rule
rules.body: A filled circle is always a state marker tinted to its state (idle / signal / danger / ok / accent). Never a bullet, an avatar frame, or decoration.

rules.name: The System-Button Rule
rules.body: Every clickable control is a .btn, a .btn.small, or a segmented cell - never a bespoke button class. A one-off header or card button skips the shared focus outline, the pointer:coarse 44px target, and the hover treatment all at once.

rules.name: The One-Lamp Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one status lamp and it always reads the whole app - never one lamp per mode, never a second indicator. Its word, not a second light, tells you which worker is live.

rules.name: The Native-Dialog Rule
rules.body: Overlays that need protected focus use <dialog> + showModal(), never a hand-rolled backdrop <div> with a JS focus trap - that pattern shipped a real focus-escape bug. A confirm that doesn't need protected focus uses the inline expand-in-place pattern.

dos: Do keep the window at exactly 100vh with overflow: hidden on both tabs; give new content a scroll region inside an existing band (The Fixed-Desk Rule).
Do lay both desks out as full-width panel bands divided by 1px line, no radius, no gutter (The Band-Not-Card Rule).
Do make every clickable control a .btn, .btn.small, or segmented cell (The System-Button Rule).
Do keep exactly one status lamp reading the whole app; let its word name the live worker (The One-Lamp Rule).
Do set every label, button, status, and numeric readout in tracked uppercase monospace (The Silkscreen Rule).
Do reserve system sans for the editor text and dialog prose, and nothing else (The Two-Voice Rule).
Do limit Signal Lavender to one primary action per view plus the live-signal surfaces (The One Signal Rule).
Do treat red as failure - a failed job, a render in flight, a destructive confirm. Signal a warning or unmet prerequisite with neutral chrome plus one danger state dot (The Failure-Is-Red Rule).
Do build depth from the bg -> panel -> panel-raised tonal ramp plus 1px borders; leave resting surfaces flat (The Flat-Desk Rule).
Do render state markers as 50%-radius circles tinted to idle / signal / danger / ok (The Circle-Means-Status Rule).
Do give every NARRATE primary action a visible kbd shortcut on its own face.
Do handle destructive confirmation inline, first focus on the safe choice, focus returned to the trigger on close.
Do keep radii at 4px for chrome, 6px for the coach bar, 8px for modals - and no radius on desk bands (The Sharp-Corner Rule).
Do drop looping and spatial motion under prefers-reduced-motion, but keep colour and opacity transitions that carry state.
Do reach for a native <dialog> + showModal() for any overlay needing protected focus (The Native-Dialog Rule).
Do give every colour-only signal a text equivalent - aria-pressed on toggles, the .vh Error: prefix, contextual aria-labels on repeated row actions.
Do duplicate the full light palette under @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) so the pre-JS first paint matches the OS.
Do hold every light-theme token at 4.5:1 against both --bg and white --panel (The Light-Theme Note).
donts: Don't let either tab scroll as a whole surface, or add a fifth band to a desk.
Don't wrap desk content in inset rounded cards with gutters between them (The Band-Not-Card Rule).
Don't create a bespoke button class for the header, a card, or anywhere else (The System-Button Rule).
Don't add a second status indicator, or split the lamp per mode (The One-Lamp Rule).
Don't use red for a warning, a hint, or a missing dependency - red is for something that failed (The Failure-Is-Red Rule).
Don't put a shadow on any part of the fixed frame - only modals, the coach bar, and toasts float (The Flat-Desk Rule).
Don't introduce a second accent hue, or use red/green on a control at rest (The State-Colour Rule).
Don't set chrome text in the sans font, or the editor/prose text in mono (The Two-Voice Rule).
Don't use uppercased monospace without letter-spacing.
Don't colour a settings section header, or any passive label, in the accent - labels are muted mono.
Don't use a filled circle as a bullet, avatar frame, or decoration (The Circle-Means-Status Rule).
Don't widen or reflow the 280px NARRATE control column.
Don't exceed an 8px corner radius, and don't reach 8px anywhere but the modal (The Sharp-Corner Rule).
Don't open a modal for a destructive confirm when an inline expand fits.
Don't hand-roll a modal backdrop <div> with a JS focus trap (The Native-Dialog Rule).
Don't build an ARIA tablist for the mode toggle - it's a group of aria-pressed toggle buttons, not tabs.
Don't dim placeholder text with extra opacity; --muted already fails contrast if dimmed further.
Don't add decorative motion; motion is for state only.
